Stock fell 13.1% on a ~$40M EBITDA guidance cut. Q4 guide still needs a big ramp (about $26M volume/mix swing, commodity recoveries, oil near $100). Free cash flow is negative year to date, and customer recovery timing is uncertain. The drop already prices much of this, so I expect only modest further underperformance.

The -10.8% drop looks like a fair reaction to a weak merchant quarter, a ZAR 261m cash outflow and leverage heading to about 3x, while the reiterated FY guidance and strong Q2 guide depend on a back-half merchant ramp and the Bank Zero approval timing, so the call adds no clear unpriced edge.

Strong Q3 and an above-Street Q4 EBITDA guide (core growth 24%, gross margin up 1,500bp, bookings up 44%) were largely priced in by the +17.5% move; offsetting this, ARR fell sequentially from attrition that management expects to last a couple more quarters, and there is no 2027 guide.

The stock fell 12.3% on a mixed print: record volume and earnings growth against higher provisions, a telecom loan charge-off, substandard assets up to 2.1% from 1.7%, Tier 1 capital ratio down to 12.9%, and data-center exposure fears. The call offers nothing clearly unpriced, and the credit worries look already reflected.

Good upstream beat, a 400 MW Temple expansion, exclusivity with an AI lab and added backstops are offset by weak power EBITDA, higher Q4 growth capex, and PPA timing risk after the Texas election, so the -8.1% move looks like it already prices this in.

Record production, 84% of Q4 oil unhedged into higher oil prices, borrowing base raised and new Permian permits point to a cash flow lift. The stock slipped 2.1% on the release, so some of this looks under-reflected, but the oil price rise is largely public and no 2027 guidance was given.

Record water volumes, a second EBITDA guidance raise and contracted growth capex setting up next year's EBITDA look under-rewarded by the -3.7% move; the offsets are heavy ABL drawn and little near-term EBITDA from the capex.
Software growth inflection (+11%) and margin beat look real, but the guide implies a Q4 slowdown, services are still weak, and the +8.7% move seems to have priced most of it in.

Strong beat: revenue +22.6%, second guidance raise to ~16% growth, new $500M revenue and $2 EPS long-term targets, and the rest of the business grew double digits. The stock was up only 4% and the Q4 guide implies a slowdown. Some of the cash flow benefit was timing, and the largest customer is a concentration risk. The call adds modest information the price may not fully reflect.

The 12.6% drop looks like a fair reaction to Q3 revenue and margin declines, a 37% fall in Google referrals and Q4 margin guidance below last year. The buybacks, $535M net cash and narrowing tech and shopping declines roughly offset that, so I see no clear unpriced information.

Shares fell 10.4% despite a raised FY adjusted operating income outlook, strong Q4 guidance, EPS growth, strong retention and a cash-funded accretive acquisition; the worries (flat CTU enrollments, legal fees, AIU calendar timing) were already flagged, so the drop looks somewhat overdone.

Large beat and raised guidance (FY revenue above $175M from above $145M, 49% adj. EBITDA margin) plus pipeline adds look mostly priced in by the +11.3% move; the ET-700 setback and conservative guidance roughly offset.

Operating results were strong (same-store NOI +15.6%, margin +230bp, occupancy +200bp) and the pipeline is active, but leverage rose to 8.1x and sequential EBITDA fell. The -11.4% drop already prices much of that, so I see a modest rebound edge.
Q3 was in line and the guidance raise, new $200M buyback and eCential robotics deal are already in the +11% move, while US hip/knee softness and a choppy market offset them.

New CEO reset: Q3 revenue missed the guide, FY revenue and EBITDA guidance came in lower, growth is slowing (top-of-funnel and organic search pressure, flat rebates, NRR 93%), and the call says it will accept near-term hits and rework the metrics it reports, yet the stock fell only 3.5%, which looks like under-reaction.

An 8.5% drop after record originations, 30% adjusted ROE, a falling net charge-off ratio and about 20% organic growth looks somewhat overdone. Rising delinquencies and acquisition costs from the broader consumer mix are already disclosed, so the edge is small.

Q4 guide and market outlook were cut (EBITDA $38-48M, Q4 adjusted EPS loss), with 4.3x leverage, the debt target pushed out, an interim CFO and price-cost still negative. The -10.5% move already prices most of this, and synergies running ahead of plan limit further downside.

Mixed call: remaining contract value +151% y/y to $440M and Aloha Next live offset by revenue guidance cut to low end, payment sites declining and restaurant SMB weakness; +3.4% move already reflects the RCV strength.

Strong Q3 beat and new wins were offset by the largest customer ending a program (about $12M Q4 hit) and a guide-up that implies a soft Q4; the 14.5% drop already reflects this, and the call adds no clear unpriced information.

Price was flat (-0.8%) despite a fast ReadyFlow conversion (~75% in six weeks), a Q4 FUROSCIX guide of about $38M (roughly double Q3), a return to profitability in Q4, and a pending FDA meeting that could speed the nintedanib trial. Offsetting this, adult Afrezza is weak and Q3 revenue was hurt by about $3M of transition effects.

The -12% move already reflects the Q3 revenue drop (-20% YoY), the slip in revenue per visit to about $3,800, and the physician collection softness. Strong visit growth (+18%), a cash build and possible 2027 guidance roughly offset these, and the IDR legislative risk is not new.

Record revenue and a buyback add-on were offset by gross margin down to 48%, rising IMS remediation costs, a growing backlog, no firm insulin biosimilar launch date and slipped filings; the +1.7% move already reflects this mixed picture.
The fee cut (about $0.03 per share of quarterly NII) and the supplemental dividend are offset by a 3.8% NAV drop, new non-accruals and a shrinking book, so the -5.5% move looks fair.

The 30% drop already prices in the Australia impairment, flat next-year revenue guide and 300-400bp margin hit from reinvestment; healthcare and ETS strength is offsetting, so I see no clear unreflected edge.

Third guidance raise, with Q3 EBITDA above the guidance range, a $20M buyback plan and bullish mining and virgin acid pricing commentary. The +5.2% move already reflects most of it, and Q4 guidance and the CFO change temper the upside.

Stock fell 14.7% on a guidance cut (EBITDA to $180-200M from customer pushouts and memory costs) plus CEO departure; much is priced in, but the cut, uncertain 2027 outlook, inventory build and no 2027 visibility point to modest drift risk, partly offset by buybacks and cash.

Capital return policy (first dividend, $100M buyback), 2026 debt maturity cleared and a strong quarter drove the +14% move, and the call adds little beyond that (Quintillion closing, capex peak, Starlink risk 'a year or more' away), so it looks largely priced in.

Beat and raise driven by ASP and TissueCypher (+47% volume), but the melanoma volume outlook was trimmed, the AD test is deprioritized with a CMS gapfill risk, and the implied Q4 guide is flat; the -9% move already seems to reflect this.

The -23.6% drop already prices in the soft Q4 exit rate, the 2026 Baxter headwind (-2 pts revenue, -4 pts EBITDA), the weak starter-set sales and 3.5x leverage, while the near-term catalysts (first 30 ARTIZEN patients in two weeks, NEXUS launch in January) roughly offset them.

Beat and raise with a second straight quarter of positive adjusted EBITDA, 20% commercial cell and gene therapy growth and an explicitly conservative Q4 guide that excludes new approvals, but the +14.4% move already prices much of it and the filing and approval outlook was trimmed from August.

NII only just covers the $0.32 dividend with the incentive fee waived (and expected to stay muted next quarter). Non-accruals rose to 4.2% at fair value and 7.3% at cost, and NAV fell 3%. Management points to spillover income as a bridge, which hints at a possible dividend cut. The -3.4% move only partly reflects this.

Record Q3 with raised 45Z carbon EBITDA outlook (at least $250M next year), a signed credit monetization deal, and a strong Q4 start, yet the stock fell 3.1%, so the call looks modestly under-reflected. Seasonal Q4 softness, corn basis risk, and 45Z policy risk limit the score.

Beat-and-raise with record margins, but Q4 revenue is guided below Q3, the selling season is slipping into Q4 with no covered-lives color for next year, and GLP-1 coverage is shrinking. The 22% drop already prices in these cautious signals, so I see no clear unpriced edge.

Stable NAV and NII covering the dividend, with the November maturity refinanced; offset by rising non-accruals, PIK up to about 10% of revenue, and a higher funding cost. Dividend is likely sustainable but headwinds are acknowledged, and the -3% move looks about right.

Record Q3 EBITDA, a completed refinancing and a $130M initial next-year outlook are offset by only 14% growth, an implied Q4 EBITDA of about $21M (below Q3), temporarily higher leverage and a choppy consumer, so the 13% drop looks roughly fair.

Routine pipeline update with cash into 2Q of the following year after a large raise. The Angel AD data slipped a quarter and the asthma start slipped slightly, both minor. The big binary catalysts (PTCL futility analysis, AD data) are still ahead of the 20-day window, and the flat price move (-0.3%) leaves nothing clearly unpriced.

Strong beat, a second guidance raise and a $1B AI-constellation win were disclosed, but the stock rose 27% and the call has little the price has missed. Q4 guide implies flat-to-lower EBITDA and lumpy pilots, and the $1B contract is only a small initial award.

The 25% drop looks larger than the largely one-off causes justify: Q1 margin hit from large low-margin deals and a fully reserved Brazil customer, with Q2-Q4 guidance held and FY raised. Offsetting this are weak organic Intelisys growth, price-driven revenue and a cash use, so the score is only modestly positive.

Stock fell only 4.5% despite 5% ARR growth, gross retention stuck in the mid-80s with no improvement, a Q4 revenue guide implying deceleration (3-4% reported growth), heavy 2026 investment and one-time costs, and rising leverage (delayed draw loan plus a $67M acquisition payment due), so the drop looks only partly priced in.

Beat and raise (FY EBITDA guide up about $8M at the midpoint, ARR add the strongest of the year, 70% incremental software margin, confident on 1H next year) supports some drift after the +8.2% move, but part of the upside is hardware pull-in, active sites were flat, and inventory is elevated.

The -9.1% drop looks like it prices in the FY EBITDA guide cut. Backlog is up 49% with no cancellations, and the implied Q4 EBITDA of $48-58M is a sharp rebound, with price-cost drag fading by Q1, so modest upside is possible. Offsetting this, the guide cut and Q3 miss raise execution risk.

NAV fell 1.8% and non-accruals rose to 3.6%, but NII covered the dividend at 115%, the dividend was held, and buybacks continue. The -4.5% move already reflects the credit worries, so I see no clear edge.

Solid beat-and-raise quarter (corporate +9.1%, NRR 104.5%, FY EPS guidance raised), but the +16.1% move already prices it in; the call has no clear unreflected information, only mild caveats (slower customer decision-making, Q4 revenue guide flat sequentially).

The -19.7% drop looks like a reaction to ARPU growth falling to 1% and a soft Q4 guide (revenue flat to slightly up sequentially, WAU flat), which offsets the real beat, WAU growth and buybacks, so I see no clear leftover mispricing.

The 22.7% drop already reflects the narrower guidance (ex-launch product sales trimmed), higher costs and falling cash ($99M vs $155M). The call shows an adequate early launch ($6.6M, refills, 88% PA approval) and an ASH R289 catalyst, which roughly offsets those, so I see no clear unpriced edge.

Guidance raise (LINZESS $1.2-1.25B, EBITDA >$350M), debt paydown and CEO transition were all disclosed on the call, and the +16.4% move likely already prices them in; no new information beyond the move.

The +18.5% move already reflects the beat, EBITDA margin expansion and lower leverage. The call adds little new: EBITDA guidance was only held despite rising commodity and fuel costs, leverage is still high at 5.5x, and organic revenue was flat.

Q3 results were strong, with Silicon Valley RevPAR up 23% and October RevPAR up 7.9%. Management called its Nov-Dec guide (low single digits) conservative, and the +3.5% move only partly prices in the room to beat. Offsetting this are tougher 2027 comps, seasonally slow Q4 and a small, illiquid REIT.
Strong AI/server growth, margin gain and in-line-to-better December guide look largely priced in after the +11.5% move, with offsetting PC/consumer weakness, so there is no clear unreflected edge.

Strong Q3 inflection with the guide pointing to FY EBITDAX well above Q3 annualized, a new buyback, and stock at under 2.5x consensus, but a +14% two-day move already prices much of it. A Grey Rock distribution overhang, a LOE and G&A guidance raise and a lowered top end of production guidance limit the upside.

Q3 EBITDA margin beat, marketplace growth and buybacks are positive, but revenue guided to the low end, websites and appraisal face headwinds, the CFO is leaving, and the +4.7% move already reflects the beat.

EBITDA beat and a second guidance raise (gross margin, tax refund) are offset by -1% air bookings, negative FCF, heavy leverage and no 2027 detail until Investor Day, so the -3.2% move looks roughly fair.

Guidance raise, the $73M DB contract exit and a $40M improvement program look largely priced in after the +16.3% move; limited residual upside from cash flow turning positive and the European restarts, with the unresolved second rail contract still a risk.

A -37.5% drop looks like an overreaction to a margin miss driven by temporary freight, resin and fuel costs, while price increases, chain-account wins and industry supply shortages should help margins, though the Q4 guide (high-single-digit EBITDA margin) is weak and uncertainty is high.

Margin and billing recovery with a loss guidance raise and higher year-end cash outlook (about $630M, near market cap) is real, but the +20.6% two-day jump has priced much of it, and revenue guidance is unchanged and implies a flat Q4, so I give only a modest positive.

Update was mildly positive (cash burn at low end of guidance, Embraer synergies, a new firm order, flight tests on track), but the stock already rose 10.1% and the backlog declined, so I see no unreflected edge.

The -19.6% drop appears to price in the guarded near-term tone (project pushouts, soft lighting and QSR, holiday seasonality). Offsetting positives are the new 3,000-store QSR award, margin initiatives, deleveraging, and a December strategic plan, so I see no clear unpriced edge.

Stock fell 8.7% on a sequential revenue dip and a large non-cash investment loss, but the call reaffirmed the $25M Q4 guide, said capacity is allocated through Q1, and left a possible Office of Strategic Capital loan as an upside catalyst. Execution risk and weak drone-sector sentiment cap the score.

The -27.4% move already prices the Q3 EBITDA miss, the Q4 guide of negative $50-100M and the liquidity cut to about $800M. The call has offsetting items: strong US pricing and a wide 2027 EBITDA range of $500-800M against unresolved debt maturities and rising costs, so I see no clear unpriced edge.

Strong Q3 and Q4 guidance (sales up ~18%, EBITDAX growth expected) look mostly priced in given the flat -0.4% move; offset by negative FCF, $239M drawn debt, hedge losses and Venus FID/CapEx uncertainty, so no clear edge.

Q4 guidance was cut hard (revenue $1.0-1.2B, Adjusted EBITDA -$7M to breakeven, legal costs and weak housing demand), but the -27.4% move already reflects it, and the call has no clearly unpriced information.

Revenue came in light, the new restructuring has at least $50M of upfront costs and the Q4 operating results will include implementation costs, and management guided to only gradual 2027 profit improvement. Offsetting that, the bookings are strong and the cost savings target is at least $100M. The -5.4% drop seems to reflect much of this already.

Record Q3 with Q4 bookings at about $21.4k/day TCE, a refinancing that saves about $2M of interest, and a confident 2027 market view, but the stock moved only +0.8%, so this is a modest under-reaction. Arctic seasonality and USTR fee risk limit the upside.

A 36% two-day drop looks larger than the call justifies: collections beat by 1%, adjusted EBITDA rose 9%, leverage fell to 2.6x, the rating outlook went to stable and legal costs are guided to fall next year. Against that, cash was flat, H2 cash growth is guided lower, and buying is shifting away from a more competitive US market, so the case for a rebound is modest.

The 25.5% drop already reflects the weak Q4 guide (Adj. EBITDA $32-38M vs ~$50M pro forma Q3) and the leveraged merger. Offsetting this are conservative housing assumptions, about $200M EBITDA if the market is flat, and $28M+ of synergies already actioned, so I see no clear unpriced edge.
Q3 beat was flattered by one-offs (crop insurance, pistachio bonus pricing), cash flow and debt concerns persist, and the turnaround plan is vague, so the +4.7% move looks roughly fair.

Q3 was solid (EBITDA +0.7%, margins up, low end of guidance raised) but the guide implies a weaker Q4 retail segment, volumes are weak and the USPP deal hasn't closed, so the -1.7% move looks about right.

Solid beat-and-raise (38% growth, guide raised to $68-70M, margin up, ample cash) but implied Q4 guide looks conservative and was already largely priced; SG&A and cash burn step up in Q4, and the -2.2% move is roughly in line with the news.

The -22.8% drop looks like a reaction to weak Q3 demand, a China royalty cut and lower guidance on royalties and net revenue, which offsets the raised full-year net income guidance and a Q4 guide above Q3; I see no clear unpriced information.

The +21.7% jump already prices in the 45Z credit upside and the $5M guidance raise, and part of the quarter was a one-time $8.3M catch-up. Offsetting that, possible Q4 restructuring charges and slow truck adoption leave no clear edge.

Deleveraging and reiterated FY guidance (sales flat to +3%, adj. EBITDA $100-110M) are offset by weak Q3 POS (units -4%, US -10%, D2C -13%), and the +2.4% move already reflects the margin and balance sheet progress.

Q3 revenue was +73% y/y and beat, and full-year guidance was raised by about the size of the beat. Growth came mostly from existing customers, gross margin was 83%, the AHA guideline inclusion and the OPPS final rule are tailwinds, and the stock was flat (-0.4%) so little of this seems priced in; heavy opex and no utilization detail limit conviction.

The -47.8% drop already prices in the capitated guidance cut (2026 target of about $220M vs $300M, a delay in statewide expansion). The Q3 EBITDA beat came from non-recurring pharmacy rebates, and the company is levered, so the large drop is not clearly an overreaction either way.

BDC with a NAV drop to $5.61, a dividend cut to $0.17, and an open-ended strategic review. The sale, markdowns and cash build were already disclosed, so the -1.6% move looks fair and no new edge is visible.

The 27.5% drop already prices in traffic of -11.5%, quarter-to-date comps of -3% with traffic flat, no price increase, and slower unit growth. The offsets are no debt, $65.6M in cash and investments, and a self-funding goal. The remaining risks are unproven value combos and a guide that needs positive comps in the back half, so the net information is balanced.

Stock fell 6.3% on a weak Q3 (funds flow -48% QoQ, wider discounts), but management says that at about $9-9.50 the share price is well below cash plus PDP value of over $12.50. The pending $1.33B asset sale, closing expected by year-end, is to be followed by a buyback (normal course and substantial issuer bid) from roughly $315M of cash, and there is Azerbaijan exploration optionality. The sell-off looks like an overreaction to backward-looking weakness, so modestly positive.

The 10.8% drop looks like a reaction to the 17% dividend cut and a 2.7% NAV decline. The call also has support the price may not fully reflect: deleveraging done ahead of target, loans sold at 99.8% of par, no new non-accruals, a pending Longview sale that could fund buybacks, and a stock at a deep discount to NAV. Offsetting this, about $0.15 of NII was hit by one-off items, David's Bridal exposure is large, and credit sentiment is weak.

Profit guidance raised, a $50M buyback was authorized, pipeline is the best of the year and the restructuring is running ahead of plan. Against that, ARR and NRR fell, the CFO/COO is leaving, 2027 revenue is guided flat, and Q3 profit was helped by $3M of savings pulled forward from Q4. The +4.9% move already reflects much of this.
